r1159104597: Shares the Eurasian landmass with Europe; the boundary between them is a historical and cultural construct rather than a clear physical divide.
Bounded by the Pacific Ocean to the east, the Indian Ocean to the south and the Arctic Ocean to the north.
Birthplace of most of the world's major religions, including Islam, Christianity, Hinduism, Buddhism and Judaism.
China and India traded places as the world's largest economy from 1 to 1800 CE, with the Silk Road as the main east-west trade route.
r1159104367: Covered almost entirely by the Antarctic ice sheet, which holds about 70% of Earth's fresh water.
Contains the geographic South Pole and is the coldest, driest and windiest continent on Earth.
First confirmed landing was by a Norwegian team in 1895, after earlier Russian, French, American and British expeditions explored its coasts.
r1159103843: An archipelago of 115 islands in the Indian Ocean, with the capital Victoria about 1,500 km east of mainland Africa.
Was uninhabited until French colonization in the 18th century, when enslaved Africans were brought to work sugar plantations.
Came under full British control in the early 19th century before later independence.
r1159104349: Non-contiguous US state bordering Canada's Yukon and British Columbia, with a maritime border with Russia across the Bering Strait.
Larger in area than Texas, California and Montana combined, making it the largest US state by far.
The Chukchi and Beaufort Seas lie to its north and the Pacific Ocean to its south.
r1730071307: A Polynesian archipelago of three reef islands and six atolls in the Pacific, roughly midway between Hawaii and Australia.
One of the world's smallest and least populated countries, with a land area of only about 25 km2.
First settled by Polynesians migrating from Samoa and Tonga around three thousand years ago.
m1159115171: A marginal sea between Europe and Asia, fed mainly by the Danube, Dnieper and Dniester rivers.
Connects to the Mediterranean via the Bosporus and Dardanelles straits.
Rimmed by the Pontic, Caucasus and Crimean Mountains, with Istanbul, Odesa and Sochi among its coastal cities.
r1159104337: Largest hot desert in the world, stretching from the Red Sea and Mediterranean coast to the Atlantic Ocean.
Bordered to the south by the Sahel, a semi-arid savanna belt along the Niger River valley.
Has alternated between desert and savanna in roughly 20,000-year cycles driven by shifts in Earth's axis.
r1159104307: Separates the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau and contains Mount Everest, the world's highest peak.
Formed by the ongoing collision of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates.
Sacred in Hinduism and Buddhism; peaks including Kailash and Gangkhar Puensum are off-limits to climbers.
Source of the Indus, Ganges and Brahmaputra rivers, whose combined basin is home to some 600 million people.
vQ1653: Flows from Germany's Black Forest through Central and Southeastern Europe to the Black Sea via the Danube Delta in Romania.
Passes four national capitals along its course: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade.
Was once a frontier of the Roman Empire and is linked to the North Sea by the Rhine-Main-Danube Canal.
r1159103479: Westernmost point and territory of the United States, the largest island in Micronesia.
Settled by the Chamorro people roughly 3,500 years ago; first reached by Europeans when Magellan landed in 1521.
Served as an important stopover for Spanish Manila galleons between the 17th and 19th centuries.
r1159104241: Bordered by the Adriatic, Ionian and Aegean Seas, the Turkish Straits and the Black Sea.
Takes its name from the Balkan Mountains, which stretch across Bulgaria.
Was largely part of the Ottoman Empire for centuries, when the region was known as Rumelia.
r1159103805: Second-largest island in the Mediterranean after Sicily, lying between the Italian Peninsula and Tunisia, just south of Corsica.
Retains traces of the prehistoric Nuragic civilization across its landscape.
Its indigenous Sardinian language is one of Italy's officially protected minority languages.
r1159103807: Fourth-largest island in the Mediterranean, lying immediately north of Sardinia.
Ruled by the Republic of Genoa for centuries before being ceded to France in 1768 and annexed in 1769.
r1159102381: A volcanic island in the Indian Ocean, part of the Mascarene Islands near Mauritius and Madagascar.
Was uninhabited until French colonization in the 17th century, which brought a plantation economy built on enslaved African labor.
As a French overseas department, it is part of the European Union and the eurozone.
r1159104115: Historical region within the Tigris-Euphrates river system, corresponding roughly to modern Iraq.
Known as the cradle of civilization, site of the Neolithic Revolution and early developments including the wheel and writing.
Home to the Sumerians, Akkadians, Assyrians and Babylonians, including the Neo-Assyrian Empire.
r1159104131: Second-largest island of the British Isles, separated from Great Britain by the Irish Sea and North Channel.
Divided between the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom.
Low-lying mountains surround a central plain, with woodland now covering only about 10% of the island.
r1159102351: Lies in the Mozambique Channel between Madagascar and the African mainland.
A French overseas department and part of the eurozone, among the most densely populated territories in the region.
Comprises a main island, Grande-Terre, and a smaller island, Petite-Terre.
p1159104835: A remote Chilean territory in the southeastern Pacific, at a corner of the Polynesian Triangle.
Famous for nearly 1,000 monumental moai statues carved by the Rapa Nui people.
The date Polynesians first settled it is debated, with estimates ranging from around 800 to 1200 CE; Chile annexed the island in 1888.
m1159115597: An extension of the Indian Ocean between the Arabian Peninsula and Iran, connected to the Gulf of Oman via the Strait of Hormuz.
Formed as the Persian Gulf Basin flooded when sea levels rose after the last glacial period.
Known for extensive fishing grounds and pearl oyster beds, though industrialization and oil spills have damaged its ecology.
r1159102805: Largest island of Greece and fifth-largest in the Mediterranean, bordering the Aegean and Libyan Seas.
Cradle of Europe's first advanced civilization, the Minoans, from around 2700 to 1420 BCE.
Later ruled successively by the Mycenaeans, Rome, the Byzantine Empire and briefly by Andalusian Arabs.
vQ3542: Main river of West Africa, rising in the Guinea Highlands and discharging through the Niger Delta into the Gulf of Guinea.
Third-longest river in Africa, after the Nile and the Congo.
Flows in a crescent shape through Mali, along Niger's border with Benin, and through Nigeria.
p1159105083: A remote Australian territory in the Indian Ocean, south of Java and Sumatra.
Named for its discovery on Christmas Day 1643; mined for phosphate deposits from the late 19th century.
Its geographic isolation has produced a high level of endemism among its flora and fauna.
p1159105105: A remote volcanic island in the South Atlantic Ocean, west of Africa and east of Brazil.
Served as a key stopover for ships rounding Africa before the Suez Canal opened in 1869.
Site of Napoleon Bonaparte's second exile, from 1815 until his death in 1821.
r1159104129: Largest of Japan's four main islands, lying between the Pacific Ocean and the Sea of Japan.
Seventh-largest island in the world and historical center of Japanese political and cultural power, including the former capitals Kyoto, Nara and Kamakura.
Home to Mount Fuji, Japan's highest mountain, and Lake Biwa, its largest lake.
r1159104353: A subregion of Oceania stretching from New Guinea to Fiji, including the Arafura Sea.
The name was coined in 1832 by French navigator Jules Dumont d'Urville alongside Micronesia and Polynesia.
Includes the independent countries of Fiji, Vanuatu, Solomon Islands and Papua New Guinea.
r1159104301: Runs north-south through Russia from the Arctic Ocean to near the Caspian Sea, forming the conventional boundary between Europe and Asia.
Highest point is Mount Narodnaya at 1,895 m, with most peaks between 1,000 and 1,300 m.
Rich in metal ores, coal and gemstones, and a major center of Russian metallurgy since the 18th century.
r1159104363: Smallest of the traditional continents, including mainland Australia, Tasmania and New Guinea.
Was joined to New Guinea and Tasmania in the single landmass Sahul until rising sea levels separated them 18,000 to 10,000 years ago.
Separated from New Guinea by the Arafura Sea and Torres Strait, and from Tasmania by the Bass Strait.
m1159116409: Shallowest sea in the world, with depths ranging from just 0.9 to 14 metres.
Connected to the Black Sea by the narrow Strait of Kerch.
Fed mainly by the Don and Kuban rivers, giving it low salinity and high fish productivity.
m1159118835: Connects the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara, straddled by the city of Istanbul.
World's narrowest strait used for international navigation.
Forms one of the continental boundaries between Asia and Europe, separating Asia Minor from Thrace.
vQ19686: Longest river entirely in England, flowing through Oxford, Reading and London to the North Sea via the Thames Estuary.
Rises at Thames Head in Gloucestershire; its lower tidal stretch through London is known as the Tideway.
Fed by at least 50 named tributaries and crossed by 45 navigation locks along its course.
m1159115305: A marginal sea between the Japanese archipelago, Sakhalin, the Korean Peninsula and the Russian Far East.
Nearly fully enclosed, giving it almost no tides, similar to the Mediterranean Sea.
Elevated dissolved oxygen levels make it highly productive for fishing.
m1159119181: A small inland sea entirely within Turkey, linking the Black Sea and Aegean Sea via the Bosporus and Dardanelles.
Separates Turkey's European and Asian sides.
Considered the smallest sea in the world, measuring roughly 280 by 80 km.
r1159102819: Largest of Spain's Balearic Islands, with Palma as its capital.
A major holiday destination, especially for tourists from the Netherlands, Germany, Ireland and the UK.
Two smaller islands, Cabrera and Dragonera, lie just off its coast.
r1159103427: Second-largest island in the Caribbean after Cuba, divided between the Dominican Republic and Haiti.
Site of the first European settlements in the Americas, including Santo Domingo.
Originally home to the Taíno and other Indigenous peoples before Spanish colonization began in 1492.
r1159104335: Sixth-largest desert in the world, spanning southern Mongolia and northern China.
A cold desert and grassland region, distinct from sandy deserts.
Its name comes from the Mongolian word for 'dryland'.
r1159104305: Stretches between the Black Sea and Caspian Sea at the intersection of Europe and Asia.
Home to Mount Elbrus, the highest peak in Europe at 5,642 metres.
Divided into the Greater Caucasus in the north and Lesser Caucasus in the south, once part of the Silk Road.
r1159104239: Fourth-largest peninsula in the world, comprising Somalia, Djibouti, Ethiopia, Eritrea and Somaliland.
Lies along the southern Red Sea, strategically important for shipping through the Gulf of Aden.
Home to the Cushitic and Ethio-Semitic speaking peoples historically known as Horn Africans.
m1159115791: Northeasternmost part of the tropical Atlantic Ocean, between Gabon and Liberia.
Contains Null Island, the notional point where the Equator meets the Prime Meridian.
Receives the Niger and Volta rivers, with a coastline including the Bight of Benin and Bight of Bonny.
vQ45403: A trans-boundary river flowing through Tibet, northeastern India and Bangladesh.
Rises near Mount Kailash as the Yarlung Tsangpo before carving great gorges through the Himalayas.
Merges with the Ganges in Bangladesh before emptying into the Bay of Bengal, and floods severely with Himalayan snowmelt.
r1159103789: Second-largest island in the Philippines, after Luzon, and seventh most populous island in the world.
Home to the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region, the country's most predominantly Islamic region.
Davao City is its largest city, followed by Zamboanga City and Cagayan de Oro.
l1159112991: Largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area, and the northernmost and highest of the Great Lakes.
Straddles the Canada-US border, bounded by Ontario, Minnesota, Michigan and Wisconsin.
Drains into Lake Huron via the St. Marys River, eventually reaching the Atlantic via the St. Lawrence River.
r1159103347: A peninsula and historical region in northwest France, homeland of the Breton people and one of the six Celtic nations.
Was an independent kingdom and duchy before uniting with the Kingdom of France in 1532.
Home to some of the world's oldest standing architecture, including the Cairn of Barnenez, dating to the early 5th millennium BC.
m1159115541: A marginal sea of the northwestern Pacific, bounded by Kamchatka, the Kuril Islands, Hokkaido and Sakhalin.
Named after the port of Okhotsk, itself named for the Okhota River.
m1159115675: Lies northwest of Norway between the North Sea and Greenland Sea, separated from the Atlantic by a ridge between Iceland and the Faroe Islands.
Mostly deep ocean floor rather than continental shelf, averaging about two kilometres deep.
Kept ice-free year-round by the warm North Atlantic Current, unlike the neighbouring Arctic seas.
l1159106765: The last and easternmost of the Great Lakes, draining into the Atlantic via the St. Lawrence River.
Shared between the Canadian province of Ontario and the US state of New York.
Its primary inlet is the Niagara River, flowing from Lake Erie.
r1159103431: A volcanic archipelago stretching from Hokkaido in Japan to Kamchatka in Russia, separating the Sea of Okhotsk from the Pacific.
Under Russian administration since the Soviet invasion in 1945.
Japan claims the four southernmost islands, fuelling the ongoing Kuril Islands dispute.
vQ602: Rises at the Rhône Glacier in Switzerland and flows through Lake Geneva into southeastern France before reaching the Mediterranean.
Forms the Camargue delta region near its mouth at Arles.
One of the three Mediterranean rivers, along with the Po and Nile, with the largest water discharge.
m1159116333: A deepwater gulf of the Indian Ocean linking the Red Sea, via the Bab-el-Mandeb strait, to the Arabian Sea.
Widening by about 15 mm a year due to tectonic activity along the Aden Ridge.
Important to ancient Greek trade and part of the Suez Canal shipping route.
r1159104007: Separates the Gulf of Mexico from the Caribbean Sea, connected to Cuba across the Yucatán Channel.
Almost entirely composed of porous limestone with low relief.
Sits on the Maya Block, the southernmost part of the North American tectonic plate.
l1159113219: An endorheic freshwater lake at the junction of Nigeria, Niger, Chad and Cameroon.
Shrank dramatically from 25,000 km2 in 1960 to just 2,000 km2 by 1980 due to climate change and water diversion.
A vital wetland ecosystem and freshwater fishery for West-Central Africa.
m1159119037: Connects the Great Lakes to the North Atlantic Ocean, flowing from Lake Ontario to the Gulf of St. Lawrence.
Has the second-highest discharge of any river in North America, after the Mississippi.
Played a key role in Canadian history and the growth of Montreal and Quebec City.
r1159104261: Spans the southern end of South America, governed by Argentina and Chile, from the Andes to the Atlantic.
Features glaciers, fjords and temperate rainforests in the west and deserts and steppes to the east.
Bounded to the south by the Strait of Magellan, Beagle Channel and Drake Passage.
vQ8493: Historically known as the Oxus, it rises in the Pamir Mountains and flows through Afghanistan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.
No longer reaches the Aral Sea, its historic terminus, due to water diversion.
Regarded in ancient times as the boundary between Greater Iran and Turan.
r1159104183: An 800-km mountain range west of the Himalayas, stretching from Afghanistan into Pakistan and Tajikistan.
Divides the Amu Darya valley to the north from the Indus River valley to the south.
A historically significant centre of Buddhism, home to the Bamiyan Buddhas.
l1159106757: The shallowest and southernmost of the Great Lakes, with its deepest point still above sea level.
Shared by Ontario and the US states of Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania and New York.
Cleveland is its largest city; the Detroit River is its primary inlet and the Niagara River its outflow.
vQ131792: One of South America's longest rivers, with a basin split mostly between Venezuela and Colombia.
Third-largest river in the world by discharge volume.
A major transportation route for the Llanos plains and interior Venezuela.
r1159102963: Scotland's northernmost archipelago, lying between Orkney, the Faroe Islands and Norway.
Its largest island, 'the Mainland', is the fifth-largest in the British Isles.
Lerwick has been its capital since 1708.
l1159114259: Lies on the Rhine at the meeting point of Germany, Switzerland and Austria.
Comprises Upper and Lower Lake Constance connected by the Seerhein stretch of the Rhine.
The exact location of the three countries' borders within the lake remains disputed.
r1159104299: A large mountain system in Central Asia whose highest peak, Jengish Chokusu, reaches 7,439 m in Kyrgyzstan.
Sacred in Tengrism, with its second-highest peak, Khan Tengri, meaning 'Lord of the Spirits'.
Its eastern and western portions are separate UNESCO World Heritage Sites, listed in 2013 and 2016.
m1159116253: A marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean between Siberia's Taymyr Peninsula and the New Siberian Islands.
Frozen most of the year, with low salinity and shallow depths mostly under 50 metres.
Named after Russian explorers Dmitry and Khariton Laptev.
m1159118553: A navigable sea route in southern Chile separating mainland South America from Tierra del Fuego.
Named after Ferdinand Magellan, whose 1520 expedition was the first European passage through it.
Shorter and more sheltered than the storm-prone Drake Passage around Cape Horn.
r1159103793: Lies about 180 km across the Taiwan Strait from mainland China's Fujian province.
Its highest peak, Yu Shan at 3,952 m, makes it the world's fourth-highest island.
The eastern two-thirds consist of rugged mountain ranges, while most of the population lives on the flatter western plains.
vQ645: Flows from Lake Ladoga to the Gulf of Finland, passing through Saint Petersburg, which was founded on its banks in 1703.
Despite its modest 74 km length, it is the fourth-largest river in Europe by average discharge.
Site of the 1240 Battle of the Neva, which gave Alexander Nevsky his name.
r1159103867: A grouping of the Caribbean's larger islands: Cuba, Hispaniola, Puerto Rico and Jamaica, plus the Cayman Islands.
Cuba is the largest island, located at the group's western end.
Together with the Lesser Antilles and Lucayan Archipelago, they form the West Indies.
m1159117337: A marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean between the New Siberian Islands and Wrangel Island.
One of the least studied Arctic seas, with shallow depths, low salinity and heavy ice cover most of the year.
Historically inhabited by Yukaghir, Chukchi, Even and Evenk peoples.
vQ882739: Originates at Lake Tana in Ethiopia and flows through Ethiopia and Sudan.
Supplies about 85.6% of the Nile's water during the rainy season, more than the White Nile.
Joins the White Nile at Khartoum to form the main Nile River.
r1159102825: A Greek island in the northeastern Aegean Sea, the third largest in Greece and eighth largest in the Mediterranean.
Separated from Asia Minor by the narrow Mytilini Strait.
Its capital, Mytilene, was founded in the 11th century BC.
vQ483159: Historically known as the Jaxartes, it rises in the Tian Shan mountains and flows toward the Aral Sea.
One of the two main rivers, along with the Amu Darya, feeding the endorheic Aral Sea basin.
Soviet-era irrigation diversions contributed to the near-disappearance of the Aral Sea.
r1159102451: A small, uninhabited atoll in the central Pacific, roughly midway between Hawaii and Australia.
Claimed as a US territory since 1857; attacked by Japan during World War II.
Made a nature preserve in the 1970s.
r1159102959: An archipelago off the north coast of Scotland, part of the Northern Isles along with Shetland.
Inhabited for at least 10,000 years, with Neolithic and Bronze Age farming settlements.
Annexed by the Kingdom of Norway in 875 before passing to the Scottish crown in 1472.
m1159116101: A shallow sea in the Indian Ocean between Timor and Australia, with the deep Sunda Trench marking its boundary with Asia.
Prone to earthquakes, tsunamis and cyclones due to its location on the Ring of Fire.
Contains significant hydrocarbon reserves that led to international disputes over the Timor Sea Treaty.
vQ10965: The longest river entirely within Spain, rising in Cantabria and flowing to the Mediterranean.
Forms a delta in the Terres de l'Ebre region of southern Catalonia.
Flows through Zaragoza, Logroño and Tortosa among other cities.
m1159115635: Bordered by the Sulu Archipelago, Mindanao, the Sangihe Islands and Sulawesi.
Formed from an ancient ocean basin roughly 42 million years ago.
Opens into the Java Sea through the Makassar Strait.
l1159126829: The largest lake in Turkey, a saline soda lake in the Armenian highlands.
An endorheic lake with no outlet, formed when a prehistoric volcanic eruption blocked its original drainage.
Holds 38% of Turkey's surface water despite high salinity usually preventing it from freezing.
r1730072495: The largest of Japan's Ryukyu Islands, about 640 km south of Kyushu.
Has been a strategic US military location since the Battle of Okinawa at the end of World War II.
Naha, on its southwest coast, is the seat of Okinawa Prefecture.
vQ4814791: The longer but less voluminous of the Nile's two major tributaries, formed from waters draining Lake Victoria.
Gets its name from the pale clay sediment it carries.
Joins the Blue Nile to form the main Nile River.
m1159115615: A deep bay of the Southern Ocean and the southernmost sea on Earth, named after explorer James Clark Ross.
Covered by the Ross Ice Shelf in its southernmost part, about 200 miles from the South Pole.
Supports a rich marine ecosystem fed by nutrient-laden circumpolar deep water.
r1159104145: A chain of volcanic islands stretching about 1,200 miles from the Alaska Peninsula toward Kamchatka.
Separates the Bering Sea from the Pacific Ocean.
Contains both the westernmost and easternmost points of the United States by longitude, since it crosses the 180th meridian.
vQ181475: The longest river in South Africa, rising in the Drakensberg mountains of Lesotho.
Forms part of South Africa's borders with both Lesotho and Namibia.
Named after the Dutch House of Orange by explorer Robert Jacob Gordon.
r1159104345: The world's largest and highest plateau, often called 'the Roof of the World'.
Surrounded by mountain ranges including the Himalayas, home to Everest and K2.
Averages over 4,500 m in elevation and feeds the headwaters of several of Asia's major rivers.
r1159103739: Spans the northernmost regions of Sweden, Finland, Norway and Russia, mostly within the Arctic Circle.
Traditional homeland of the Sámi people and home to Rovaniemi's Santa Claus Village.
r1159102965: An Aegean archipelago southeast of mainland Greece, named for the islands ringing the sacred island of Delos.
Naxos is the largest island, while Syros is the most populated.
m1159117819: A sea between Denmark and Sweden where the Baltic Sea drains through the Danish Straits.
Shallow and dangerous to navigate due to sandy reefs and shifting currents; Gothenburg and Aarhus are its largest ports.
r1159104147: An island subregion comprising the Greater Antilles, Lesser Antilles and Lucayan Archipelago.
Includes 13 independent countries and 18 dependencies; the term is often used interchangeably with 'Caribbean'.
m1159115655: Separated from the South China Sea by Palawan and from the Celebes Sea by the Sulu Archipelago.
Home to the Tubbataha Reef, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
r1159104275: A chain of volcanic islands formed by the Hawaiian hotspot on the Pacific Plate, part of the Hawaiian-Emperor seamount chain.
About 1,860 miles from the nearest continent, among the most isolated major island groups on Earth.
The US state of Hawaii is the only state entirely on an archipelago and not geographically connected to North America.
r1159102667: Largest island and capital of the Northern Mariana Islands, a US territory in the western Pacific.
Passed through Spanish, German and Japanese rule before the US took control after the Battle of Saipan in World War II.
r1159103915: A mountain range along India's west coast, formed when India separated from Africa during the breakup of Gondwana.
Runs almost continuously from the Tapti River to Kanyakumari, meeting the Eastern Ghats at the Nilgiris.
p1159105049: Southernmost headland of the Tierra del Fuego archipelago, marking where the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans meet.
First rounded in 1616 by Dutch navigators Willem Schouten and Jacob Le Maire.
Known for hazardous waters with strong winds, currents and icebergs; a major clipper-ship route until the Panama Canal opened in 1914.
r1159103077: Separates Turkey's Mediterranean coast from the central Anatolian Plateau.
Part of the Alpide mountain belt, extending from Lake Eğirdir to the upper Euphrates and Tigris rivers.
l1159113577: One of the African Great Lakes, lying in the Albertine Rift between the DR Congo and Rwanda.
One of only three lakes known to undergo limnic eruptions, releasing dissolved carbon dioxide from its depths.
Volcanic activity about 10,000 years ago reversed its drainage, cutting it off from the Nile watershed.
m1159116715: Connects the Great Lakes to the Atlantic Ocean via the St. Lawrence River.
Fringed by Quebec, the Maritime provinces and Newfoundland, plus France's Saint-Pierre and Miquelon.
r1730073425: Stretches along Iran's Caspian Sea coast, part of the Alpide mountain belt.
Home to Mount Damavand, Iran's highest peak.
vQ3411: Canada's longest river system, flowing from Great Slave Lake to the Arctic Ocean.
Drains about 20% of Canada's land area, the largest river system flowing into the Arctic from North America.
r1159102379: Second-largest of Spain's Canary Islands, located about 97 km off North Africa.
Geologically the oldest island in the Canary archipelago; declared a UNESCO biosphere reserve in 2009.
r1159102757: One of Indonesia's Lesser Sunda Islands, named by Portuguese explorers for its flowers.
Lies near Komodo and Rinca islands, home to the Komodo dragon.
e1159105649: Highest peak in Iran and Western Asia, a dormant stratovolcano in the Alborz range.
Holds special significance in Persian mythology and folklore.
Part of the Volcanic Seven Summits mountaineering challenge.
vQ78879: Flows through northeastern Siberia, frozen for about 250 days each year.
Its basin spans the Sakha Republic, Chukotka and Magadan Oblast in Russia's Far East.
m1159116451: A sea off northern Australia, bounded by Cape York Peninsula and Arnhem Land.
Was dry land connecting Australia to New Guinea during the last ice age, when sea levels were far lower.
Hosts a submerged coral reef province discovered only recently.
r1159102673: Part of French Polynesia's Society Islands, centred on the remnants of an extinct volcano.
Surrounded by a lagoon and barrier reef; a major luxury tourist destination.
vQ192415: Ghana's main river system, formed from the Black, White and Red Volta.
Dammed at Akosombo to create Lake Volta, the largest man-made reservoir by area in the world.
Burkina Faso was once named Upper Volta after the river.
r1159104071: Australia's largest desert, spanning Western Australia and South Australia.
A sparsely populated ecoregion and interim bioregion.
e1159107539: Highest mountain peak of any island on Earth, located in Indonesia's Sudirman Range on New Guinea.
One of the Seven Summits, with an elevation exceeding the highest peaks of Papua New Guinea, New Zealand and Australia.
Ranked 5th in the world by topographic isolation.
vQ8187: Flows through northern Russia into the White Sea's Dvina Bay.
Drains much of Northwest Russia into the Arctic Ocean alongside the Pechora River.
e1159105413: Largest mountain massif in Antarctica, within the Sentinel Range of the Ellsworth Mountains.
Contains Mount Vinson, Antarctica's highest peak at 4,892 m, first climbed in 1966.
Named after US congressman Carl Vinson for his support of Antarctic exploration.
m1159118385: An intertidal zone in the southeastern North Sea, stretching along the Frisian Islands from the Netherlands to Denmark.
A vital breeding and migration habitat for birds; a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2009.
Historically prone to catastrophic floods, including the Saint Marcellus' floods of 1219 and 1362.
r1159104151: Forms the northernmost part of mainland Eurasia, in Russia's Far North.
r1159103821: Largest chain of atolls in the world, part of French Polynesia.
Major islands include Rangiroa, Anaa and Fakarava, inhabited by Polynesians who settled the archipelago.
l1159106747: 12th largest lake on Earth and Canada's sixth-largest freshwater lake, north of the city of Winnipeg.
Its eastern shore's boreal forests were inscribed as the Pimachiowin Aki UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2018.
Used by Manitoba Hydro as one of the world's largest hydroelectric reservoirs.
vQ142148: Longest river running entirely within Brazil, originating in the Canastra mountain range.
Known locally as 'Velho Chico' ('Old Frank'); it empties into the Atlantic between Alagoas and Sergipe.
r1159103661: Easternmost point of continental Asia, in Russia's Far East.
Known as Chukotka, home to the Indigenous Chukchi people.
l1159106721: Largest lake entirely within Canada and the eighth-largest in the world, on the Arctic Circle in the Northwest Territories.
Named for the Sahtu Dene people, whose name means 'grizzly bear-water people'.
Drains via the Great Bear River into the Mackenzie River.
m1159116205: Connects the Labrador Sea to Baffin Bay between Greenland and Baffin Island.
Named after English explorer John Davis, who searched for the Northwest Passage; later used for whale hunting.
r1159103865: A remote Russian Arctic archipelago between the East Siberian and Laptev Seas.
m1159118281: Separates New Zealand's North and South Islands, connecting the Tasman Sea to the South Pacific.
Named after James Cook, the first European to sail through it, in 1770.
Known for strong, unpredictable tidal flows and several historic shipwrecks.
r1159103833: Second-largest island in the Hawaiian archipelago, dominated by the Haleakalā volcano and the West Maui Mountains.
The two volcanic areas are joined by a narrow isthmus, giving Maui its nickname 'the Valley Isle'.
Lahaina, a historic town on the island, was largely destroyed by fire in 2023.
l1159126725: Largest lake in China, an alkaline endorheic salt lake in Qinghai Province.
Shrank for much of the 20th century but has grown again since 2004.
xQ213360: A flat-topped mountain overlooking Cape Town, South Africa.
Home to over 2,000 plant species, roughly 80% of them fynbos.
Table Mountain National Park is South Africa's most visited national park.
r1159104075: Covers parts of Jordan, Syria, Iraq and Saudi Arabia, merging south into the Arabian Desert.
Accounts for about 85% of Jordan's land area and 55% of Syria's.
r1159103847: A Russian Arctic archipelago off Siberia's Taymyr Peninsula, separating the Kara and Laptev Seas.
The last sizeable archipelago on Earth to be discovered, first charted in 1930-1932.
Home to the Academy of Sciences Glacier, the largest glacier in Russia.
m1159116797: Highest tidal range in the world, averaging about 16 m due to tidal resonance in its funnel-shaped basin.
About 100 billion tonnes of water flow in and out every half-day tidal cycle, twice the combined flow of the world's rivers.
Lies between New Brunswick and Nova Scotia, an arm of the Gulf of Maine.
r1159102433: Atoll capital of Kiribati in the central Pacific's Micronesia region.
Site of the Battle of Tarawa during World War II.
South Tarawa holds about half the country's entire population.
r1730072791: A mountain range in the Sahara desert in southeastern Algeria, whose name means 'plateau of rivers'.
Holds one of the world's most important groupings of prehistoric cave art.
A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1982.
p1159104849: A Leeward Island in the Caribbean, the most populous island of Antigua and Barbuda.
Home to English Harbour's Nelson's Dockyard, a UNESCO World Heritage Site named after Vice-Admiral Horatio Nelson.
St. John's, its capital, has a deep harbour able to accommodate large cruise ships.
r1159102761: One of Indonesia's Lesser Sunda Islands, between Lombok and Flores.
Traditionally known as a source of sappanwood, honey and sandalwood.
Marks a cultural boundary between islands influenced by Indian religions to the west and those less influenced to the east.
r1159104139: An Indian archipelago in the eastern Indian Ocean, separated from Thailand by the Andaman Sea.
Forms a maritime boundary between the Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea alongside the Andaman Islands.
Great Nicobar Island was added to UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves in 2013.
p1159105093: An uninhabited volcanic island in the Bellingshausen Sea, claimed as a dependency of Norway.
Nearly entirely covered by glacier and surrounded by pack ice most of the year.
First sighted in 1821 by Fabian von Bellingshausen; no one set foot on it until 1929.
e1159107729: Highest mountain in New Zealand, in the Southern Alps of the South Island.
Consists of three summits: the Low Peak, Middle Peak and High Peak.
Ranked 10th in the world by topographic isolation.
r1159102767: An Indonesian island off the northeastern coast of Java, part of East Java province.
Separated from Java by the narrow Madura Strait.
vQ193737: Flows through Tennessee, Alabama, Mississippi and Kentucky, beginning at the confluence of the French Broad and Holston rivers in Knoxville.
The largest tributary of the Ohio River.
r1159103983: Second largest river delta in Europe, after the Volga Delta, and the continent's best preserved.
Lies mostly in Romania where the Danube empties into the Black Sea, with a small part in Ukraine.
Its combined territory with the Razim-Sinoe lagoons is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
l1159113563: The largest trans-boundary lake in Europe, lying on the Estonia-Russia border.
Fifth-largest lake in Europe, after Ladoga, Onega, Vänern and Saimaa.
Comprises three connected basins: Lake Peipus, Lake Pskov and the Warm Lake channel between them.
m1159117919: Connects the Sea of Japan with the Pacific Ocean between Honshu and Hokkaido.
The Seikan Tunnel passes beneath it at its narrowest point, about 19.5 km.
Japan limits its territorial waters here to three nautical miles to allow US nuclear-armed vessels through.
l1159115641: The largest freshwater lake in Japan, located in Shiga Prefecture near Kyoto.
An ancient lake, over 4 million years old and estimated to be the 13th oldest lake in the world.
Frequently referenced in Japanese literature and poetry due to its proximity to Kyoto.
r1159103253: The largest salt flat in the world, in southwestern Bolivia near the crest of the Andes.
Formed from the desiccation of ancient Pleistocene lakes, leaving an 8-metre-thick salt crust.
Rich in lithium brine beneath its surface; after rain it becomes the world's largest mirror.
r1159103411: The third-largest island in the Mediterranean, after Sicily and Sardinia.
Dominated by the Troodos Mountains and the Kyrenia Range, separated by the Mesaoria plain.
Has experienced Greek, Byzantine, Ottoman and British influence over its long history.
r1159103827: Largest island in the Solomon Islands by area and population.
Site of the major Guadalcanal campaign between Japanese and Allied forces in 1942-43.
Honiara, its north coast town, became the capital of the British Solomon Islands after World War II.
m1159117355: A body of water in the Arctic Ocean between Canada's Ellesmere Island and Greenland.
Covered year-round by the thickest sea ice in the Arctic Ocean, up to 15 m thick.
Named after Robert Todd Lincoln during an 1881-1884 US Arctic expedition.
r1159103095: A mountain subprovince of the Bohemian Massif shared by the Czech Republic, Poland and Germany.
Its highest peak, Sněžka, is also the highest point in Bohemia and Silesia.
e1159105865: The highest mountain in Bhutan and the highest unclimbed mountain in the world.
Its name means 'White Peak of the Three Spiritual Brothers' in Dzongkha.
Mountaineering has been entirely banned in Bhutan since 2003.
r1159103389: The largest island of Indonesia's Maluku province, north of the historically significant Ambon Island.
Located near the Banda Islands and other smaller islands.
r1159103611: Contains Mulhacén, the highest point in continental Spain at 3,479 m.
A popular ski destination near the Mediterranean coast, despite the region's otherwise hot climate.
Home to the Sierra Nevada and Calar Alto astronomical observatories.
e1159105945: The highest mountain in Austria and in the Alps east of the Brenner Pass.
Its pyramid-shaped summit consists of two pinnacles, the Großglockner and Kleinglockner.
The Pasterze, Austria's longest glacier, lies on its eastern slope.
m1159117937: Divides Russia's Sakhalin Island from the Asian mainland, connecting the Sea of Okhotsk to the Sea of Japan.
Extremely shallow at its narrowest point, only about 4 m deep.
r1159102847: A group of islands off mainland Tanzania, also known as the Spice Islands.
Main islands include Unguja (Zanzibar Island), Pemba and Mafia.
Most of the archipelago forms Zanzibar, a semi-autonomous region of Tanzania.
r1159104505: Divides East and West Antarctica, stretching from Cape Adare to Coats Land.
First sighted by the British Ross expedition in 1841 and first crossed in 1901-1904.
e1159108379: An active stratovolcano at the northern end of Martinique in the Lesser Antilles.
Its 1902 eruption destroyed the town of Saint-Pierre, killing around 29,000-30,000 people in the worst volcanic disaster of the 20th century.
Became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2023.
r1159102815: The largest and most populous island of the Maltese Archipelago, south of Italy and north of Libya.
Valletta is its capital, with the landscape characterised by low hills and terraced fields.
l1159113373: The largest freshwater lake in Mongolia by volume, nicknamed 'Mother Sea'.
Second-largest lake in the country by area, after Uvs Lake.
m1159117223: Lies in Canada's Northwest Territories, explored by Roald Amundsen between 1903 and 1906.
Marks the western end of the Northwest Passage between the Atlantic and Pacific.
r1159102873: An uninhabited Canadian Arctic island, part of the Sverdrup and Queen Elizabeth Islands.
Known for unusual fossilised forests dating from the Eocene period.
r1159103449: A large island in Papua New Guinea's Bismarck Archipelago, named after the island of Ireland.
Separated from New Britain by Saint George's Channel.
Was renamed Neumecklenburg during the German New Guinea colonial period.
p1159105007: Site of the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station and near the Kennedy Space Center, on Florida's Space Coast.
Separated from Merritt Island by the Banana River.
Home to Port Canaveral, one of the busiest cruise ports in the world.
m1159117043: The largest estuary in the United States, separated from the Atlantic by the Delmarva Peninsula.
More than 150 rivers and streams feed its drainage basin, spanning six states and Washington, D.C.
Stretches about 200 miles from the Susquehanna River to the Atlantic Ocean.
r1730070733: Straddles the border between Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with permanently snow-capped and glaciated peaks.
One of the sources of the Nile, historically linked by European explorers to Ptolemy's legendary 'Mountains of the Moon'.
r1159102943: Part of the Aleutian Islands chain in the Russian Far East, east of the Kamchatka Peninsula.
Treeless and sparsely populated, consisting mainly of Bering Island and Medny Island.
e1159106519: The highest of the Pacaraima chain of flat-topped tepuis, at the junction of Brazil, Guyana and Venezuela.
Surrounded by cliffs 400-1,000 m high, home to much endemic flora and fauna due to its isolation.
First climbed by a British expedition in 1884.
r1159103087: A mountain range in northern Greece and southern Albania, known colloquially as the 'spine of Greece'.
Geologically an extension of the Dinaric Alps that dominate the western Balkans.
p1159105063: A small, uninhabited tropical atoll in the Mozambique Channel, claimed by both France and Madagascar.
Garrisoned by a French detachment and visited mainly by scientists studying its green sea turtle breeding grounds.
l1159125149: The largest artificial reservoir in the world by surface area, formed behind the Akosombo Dam.
Generates a substantial share of Ghana's electricity and lies entirely within the country.
r1159102871: An uninhabited Arctic island in Nunavut, part of the Arctic Archipelago between Victoria Island and Somerset Island.
Lies south of the Queen Elizabeth Islands, with no permanent settlements.
r1159104617: The third-largest and southernmost inhabited island of New Zealand, separated from the South Island by Foveaux Strait.
Over 80% of the island forms Rakiura National Park.
Most residents live in the small settlement of Oban.
e1159105985: A mountain massif on the Italy-Switzerland border in the Pennine Alps.
Its main summit, the Dufourspitze, is the second-highest peak in the Alps and western Europe, after Mont Blanc.
Its northwestern face holds one of the largest Alpine glaciers, near Zermatt.
vQ8542: A tributary of the Amu Darya forming much of the Afghanistan-Tajikistan border.
Formed by the confluence of the Pamir and Wakhan rivers near Qala-i-Panjah.
Served as a strategic river during Soviet military operations in Afghanistan in the 1980s.
r1159102771: Indonesia's 9th largest island, east of Sumatra, home to the provincial capital Pangkal Pinang.
Its tin mining industry has caused considerable environmental damage on and offshore.
r1159102601: An archipelago in the South China Sea controlled by China but disputed by Taiwan and Vietnam.
Comprises about 130 small coral islands and reefs, mostly in the Amphitrite and Crescent Groups.
Its name comes from the Portuguese word for a submerged reef.
e1159105901: The highest peak in the High Tatras, Slovakia and the entire Carpathian Mountains.
Has had four different names amid 20th-century geopolitical changes affecting Hungary, Czechoslovakia and Slovakia.
Rises about 2,000 m above the valley floor.
r1159102745: The third largest island in Indonesia's Maluku Islands, between the Banda and Seram Seas.
Home to the indigenous Buru people alongside several smaller ethnic groups.
Most of the island is covered by tropical forest rich in endemic bird and mammal species.
r1159103387: The largest island of the Chiloé Archipelago off southern Chile's Pacific coast.
A geological continuation of the Chilean Coast Range, with the Sea of Chiloé submerging part of the Central Valley.
Its landscape includes rolling hills, forests and many coastal inlets and bays.
r1159104217: A vast semiarid lowland spanning Bolivia, Paraguay and Argentina, South America's second-largest forested ecoregion.
Home to over 3,400 plant species and animals including jaguars and giant armadillos.
Sparsely inhabited for centuries by Indigenous peoples including the Wichí, Qom and Guaraní.
e1159105939: Highest peak in Bulgaria, the Rila Mountains and the entire Balkan Peninsula.
Within Rila National Park, one of the easiest places in Europe to see the wallcreeper bird.
A cosmic ray research station was built on its summit in 1960.
vQ171840: Also called the Caquetá River, it rises in Colombia and flows through Brazil to join the Amazon.
One of the Amazon basin's major tributaries at 2,820 km long.
r1159102691: Tonga's main island and home to its capital, Nukuʻalofa.
The most populous island in the country, with about 70% of Tonga's total population.
Has developed as the nation's business and trade centre.
r1159103899: A mountain range in Russia's Sakha Republic, near the famously frigid settlement of Verkhoyansk.
Part of the East Siberian Mountains, lying near the Eurasian-North American tectonic plate boundary.
Contains coal, silver, lead, tin and zinc deposits.
vQ269710: The longest river entirely within British Columbia, Canada, rising near Blackrock Mountain in the Rockies.
Flows into the Strait of Georgia just south of Vancouver.
Discharges about 20 million tons of sediment into the ocean each year.
r1159102373: One of Cape Verde's sandy eastern islands, known for white sand beaches and over 350 days of sunshine a year.
Hosts the second-largest rookery for Caretta (loggerhead) turtles in Cape Verde, the world's largest nesting aggregation for the species.
r1159102903: A French Polynesian archipelago at the southeast end of the Tuamotu chain, culturally closer to the Marquesas Islands.
Made up of the volcanic Mangareva Islands and the uninhabited Temoe atoll.
e1159105269: The highest peak in Morocco, the Atlas Mountains, North Africa and the Arab world.
Visible from Marrakesh, about 63 km to the north.
The highest peak for over 2,000 km in any direction.
vQ49544: A southeastern tributary of the Amazon in northern Brazil, one of the largest clearwater rivers in the Amazon basin.
Accounts for about 5% of the Amazon's total water volume.
m1159120183: A small sea in the Philippines separating Luzon from the Visayas.
Its southern part is nicknamed 'the Galápagos of Asia' for its isolation and biodiversity.
r1159104161: The largest area of contiguous endorheic (no ocean outlet) watersheds in North America, spanning Nevada, Utah and parts of neighbouring states.
Contains both the lowest point in the contiguous US, Badwater Basin, and nearby Mount Whitney, the highest.
r1159104539: Two uninhabited subantarctic volcanic islands in the southern Indian Ocean, administered by South Africa.
Named Marion Island and Prince Edward Island; protected as Special Nature Reserves and a marine protected area.
Home only to staff of a South African research station on Marion Island.
p1159105071: A rugged volcanic island in the South Atlantic, a dependency of Tristan da Cunha.
One of the most remote places with a constant human presence, home only to weather station personnel since 1956.
Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site 'Gough and Inaccessible Islands', one of the world's most important seabird colonies.
e1159105915: The highest mountain in the Pyrenees and Spain's third-highest peak.
Its northern side holds the largest glacier in the Pyrenees, which has lost more than half its surface in the last 100 years and may disappear by 2050.
l1159114155: The largest lake on the island of Ireland and in the British Isles.
Supplies about 40.7% of Northern Ireland's drinking water.
Has suffered pollution from blue-green algae blooms since 2023.
r1159102393: A remote, uninhabited Canadian Arctic island, the westernmost of the Queen Elizabeth Islands.
Historically icebound year-round, making it one of the least accessible parts of Canada.
First sighted by Europeans in 1853 during the Edward Belcher expedition.
r1159104063: Part of the eastern Sahara, lying between the Nile River and the Red Sea in Sudan.
The Nile passes through most of its cataracts as it crosses the desert.
Historically crossed by ancient Egyptian traders seeking gold and goods from Nubia.
l1159113611: The third-largest freshwater lake entirely within China, in the Yangtze Delta.
Contains about 90 islands and is linked to the Grand Canal.
Surrounded by the major cities of Suzhou, Wuxi, Changzhou and Huzhou.
r1159102679: The sixth-largest of the Hawaiian Islands, nicknamed 'the Pineapple Island' for its past as an island-wide plantation.
About 98% of the island is owned by Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison.
Separated from Molokaʻi by the Kalohi Channel and from Maui by the Auʻau Channel.
r1730074339: An entirely volcanic Antarctic island on the east side of McMurdo Sound.
Home to Mount Erebus, an active volcano, and the extinct Mount Terror.
Site of the US McMurdo Station, the largest human settlement in Antarctica.
e1159106827: The highest mountain in Wales and in the British Isles south of the Scottish Highlands.
Shaped by Ordovician-period volcanic rock and extensively sculpted by glaciation.
Among the busiest mountains in the UK, climbed by over 540,000 walkers in 2022; also reachable by the Snowdon Mountain Railway.
vQ117615: Unites with the Madre de Dios River to form the Madeira, a major Amazon tributary.
Rises on the northern slope of the Sierra de Cochabamba in Bolivia.
r1159102555: Located in the Bering Sea, closer to Russia and Asia than to mainland Alaska.
Thought to be one of the last exposed remnants of the Pleistocene land bridge between Asia and North America.
Jointly owned by the Siberian Yupik villages of Gambell and Savoonga.
r1159103647: Australia's fifth-largest desert, located in Western Australia in an almost pristine state.
Home to a small group of Indigenous Australians.
r1159102585: An island group in the Caroline Islands of the western Pacific, part of the Federated States of Micronesia.
The name also refers to the broader Yap State, including its outer islands.
e1159105701: A sacred Buddhist site in Shanxi Province, China, surrounded by flat-topped peaks.
Home to over 53 monasteries and temples, making it one of China's most important Buddhist sites.
A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2009.
vQ2279579: The largest river in Malawi, the only outlet of Lake Malawi, flowing into the Zambezi River in Mozambique.
Passes Kapachira Falls and large hippopotamus populations in Liwonde National Park.
David Livingstone travelled up the river during his Second Zambezi expedition in 1859.
m1159116571: A wide Mediterranean embayment along the coasts of Catalonia, Languedoc-Roussillon and Provence.
Known for the cold, blustery Mistral and Tramontane winds.
r1159102561: A sparsely populated island in Quebec, Canada, within the Gulf of St. Lawrence.
Separated from mainland Quebec by the Jacques Cartier and Honguedo straits.
r1159103641: The largest hot desert in North America, spanning northern Mexico and the southwestern United States.
Its largest expanse lies in the Mexican state of Chihuahua.
A geologically young desert, existing for only about 8,000 years.
r1159104369: Makes up two-thirds of the Antarctic continent, separated from West Antarctica by the Transantarctic Mountains.
Contains the geographic South Pole and the Gamburtsev Mountain Range, buried under its ice sheet.
Supports breeding colonies of penguins, seabirds and several seal species along its coasts.
l1159126453: A shallow, highly saline endorheic lake in Southern California, lying on the San Andreas Fault.
Formed repeatedly over centuries as the Colorado River alternately flowed into or diverted around the Salton Trough, drying completely around 1580.
Became a resort destination in the 20th century before suffering fish and bird die-offs from farm runoff contamination.
vQ3047: Formed by the joining of the North and South Saskatchewan Rivers near Prince Albert, flowing east into Lake Winnipeg.
Its watershed, including tributaries, stretches to the Rocky Mountains in Alberta.
r1159102675: A volcanic island in French Polynesia, 17 km northwest of Tahiti, part of the Society Islands.
Formerly known as ʼAimeho; early Western visitors also called it York Island.
r1159103279: Australia's fourth-largest desert, spanning the Northern Territory, South Australia and Queensland.
Contains the world's longest parallel sand dunes, including the 40 m Big Red dune.
Underlain by the Great Artesian Basin, one of the largest inland drainage systems in the world.
r1159104173: A mountain range in Russia's Sakha Republic and Amur Oblast, also known as the Outer Khingan Range.
First scientifically described by Russian researcher Alexander von Middendorff.
p1159104689: The most westerly point of mainland England and the most south-westerly point in Great Britain.
A popular tourist destination on Cornwall's Penwith peninsula, between the English Channel and the Celtic Sea.
e1159105927: The highest peak in the Southern Ural Mountains, within Russia's South Ural Nature Reserve.
Rumoured by US officials to house a large secret underground bunker complex.
l1159106953: A large freshwater lake lying mostly between New York and Vermont, extending north into Quebec.
Nicknamed 'The Sixth Great Lake' for its connections to the St. Lawrence Seaway and the Hudson River via canal.
Historic Fort Ticonderoga lies near its southern end.
xQ38519: A waterfall in the canyon of Iceland's Hvítá river, one of the country's most popular tourist attractions.
A key stop on 'Golden Circle' tours near Reykjavík.
r1159102725: Part of the New Siberian Islands' Anzhu subgroup, between the Laptev and East Siberian Seas.
One of the 50 largest islands in the world, connected to Faddeyevsky Island by the low-lying Bunge Land.
r1159103699: A geo-cultural highland region covering northern Arkansas and southern Missouri.
The most extensive highland region between the Appalachians and the Rocky Mountains.
Includes the Boston Mountains and the ancient St. Francois Mountains.
p1159105011: A resort city at the southern tip of Mexico's Baja California peninsula.
Known for its sea arch, El Arco, scuba diving and marine wildlife including marlin and sharks.
Forms the Los Cabos metro area together with neighbouring San José del Cabo.
l1159126775: The largest lake in Turkmenistan, lying roughly midway between the Caspian and Aral Seas.
Historically fed by the Uzboy River, a former Amu Darya distributary; now sustained mainly by an irrigation canal.
r1159102657: An island in Vanuatu's Shefa Province, home to the capital city, Port Vila.
Originally named Sandwich Island by early European explorers.
r1159103729: A vast semi-arid plateau in eastern Ethiopia, overwhelmingly inhabited by Somali people.
Known for oil and gas reserves and over a century of Somali self-determination movements.
Represents the westernmost region inhabited by Somalis in the Horn of Africa.
e1159106007: Hungary's highest mountain, in the Mátra range.
The country's third most popular tourist attraction after Lake Balaton and the Danube, with skiing pistes and a TV tower at its summit.
e1159106091: One of Mexico and North America's most active volcanoes, part of the Colima Volcanic Complex.
Has erupted more than 40 times since 1576, with one of its largest eruptions in 1913.
Most of its surface actually lies in Jalisco state rather than Colima, despite its name.
l1159114299: An endorheic lake in southwestern Tanzania's Rukwa Valley.
The third largest inland body of water in the country.
m1159120779: A large bay of the Bering Sea in far northeastern Siberia.
One of the easternmost bays in Russia, opening onto the Bering Sea close to Alaska.
r1159103613: Stretches across southern Spain, forming the southern edge of the Meseta Central plateau.
Separates the Guadiana river valley to the north from the Guadalquivir valley to the south.
Steeped in Spanish legend, including tales of bandits and a child raised by wolves.
l1159113395: The second largest lake in Finland, draining into the Gulf of Finland via the Kymi River.
An underground aqueduct, the Päijänne Water Tunnel, supplies drinking water to the Greater Helsinki area.
Jyväskylä is the largest city on its shores.
vQ3292: Drains Lake Winnipeg and empties into Hudson Bay near Port Nelson.
Including its Saskatchewan and Bow River headwaters, its full length reaches about 2,575 km.
m1159117021: Bounded by Cape Cod in Massachusetts and Cape Sable Island in Nova Scotia.
Includes Massachusetts Bay, Penobscot Bay and the Bay of Fundy as arms of the gulf.
Named after the English colonial Province of Maine.
r1730073379: A mountain range in Russia's Transbaikal region, forming the primary watershed between the Arctic and Pacific Oceans.
Rich in tin deposits, with the Trans-Siberian Railroad passing through.
Mongolia's capital, Ulaanbaatar, lies at the range's southwestern edge.
l1159125055: The world's largest artificial lake and reservoir by volume, on the Zambezi River between Zambia and Zimbabwe.
Filled between 1958 and 1963 after the Kariba Dam flooded the Kariba Gorge.
Displaced communities led to the growth of towns including Kariba, Siavonga and Binga.
r1159102615: A Moroccan mountain range, the northernmost and second highest of the country's three Atlas chains.
Separated from the High Atlas by the Moulouya and Um Er-Rbiâ rivers.
Native habitat of the Barbary macaque.
r1159103679: Also known as Saurashtra, a peninsula in Gujarat, India, bordering the Arabian Sea.
Bounded by the Gulf of Kutch to the northwest and the Gulf of Khambhat to the east.
Its ports have been trading centres since at least the 16th century.
l1159113513: Also called Dalai Lake, a large lake in China's Inner Mongolia region.
One of the largest lakes in China, lying amid the grasslands of Inner Mongolia near the Mongolian border.
r1730072769: A historic region in southern Arabia, spanning Yemeni governorates and parts of Oman and Saudi Arabia.
Home to the Hadharem people, who historically spoke the ancient Hadramautic language.
Stretches from the Empty Quarter desert toward the Arabian Sea coast.
l1159106833: The largest lake entirely within Ontario, Canada, part of the Great Lakes drainage basin.
Drains into Lake Superior via the Nipigon River.
r1159103197: A large peninsula in Southcentral Alaska, named after the Kahtnuht'ana Dena'ina people who historically inhabited the area.
Its name derives from 'Kenaitze,' meaning the local Athabascan tribe.
r1159104095: The narrowest part of the Malay Peninsula, in southern Thailand.
At its narrowest point, only 44 km separates the Andaman Sea from the Gulf of Thailand.
Marks the boundary between the Phuket Range and the mountain chain running from Tibet.
l1159124989: A former reservoir on Ukraine's Dnieper River, created in 1956 by the Kakhovka Dam.
Completely drained after the dam was breached in June 2023 during the Russian invasion of Ukraine.
m1159118329: Located on the southern coast of New Guinea, part of Papua New Guinea's coastline.
Receives the outflow of the Fly River, one of New Guinea's largest rivers.
r1730073315: A sub-range of the Atlas Mountains, mainly in Algeria with its eastern end reaching Tunisia.
Its summits are more rugged than the parallel, coast-hugging Tell Atlas range.
r1159104037: A wide flood basalt plateau spanning Washington, Oregon and Idaho.
Lies between the Cascade Range and the Rocky Mountains, cut through by the Columbia River.
xQ38161: The widest waterfall in the world, on the Mekong River in southern Laos near Cambodia.
The main reason the Mekong is not navigable into China.
Characterised by thousands of islands, giving the area its name 'Si Phan Don,' or '4,000 islands.'
l1159114641: A Patagonian trough lake in Argentina's Santa Cruz province, formed by melting glacial ice.
The second largest perennial lake entirely within Argentina, fed by the Viedma Glacier.
Near the town of El Chaltén and the Andes peaks Cerro Torre and Fitz-Roy.
r1159102979: The northern part of Namibia's Atlantic coast, called 'The Land God Made in Anger' by the indigenous San people.
Known for dense ocean fogs from the cold Benguela current and constant heavy surf.
Features high sand dunes north of Terrace Bay and gravel plains to the south.
r1159104437: The highest mountain ranges in Antarctica, containing Mount Vinson, the continent's highest point at 4,892 m.
Split by the Minnesota Glacier into the Sentinel Range and Heritage Range.
Lie within the Chilean Antarctic territorial claim.
xQ1130718: A waterfall on the Skógá River in southern Iceland, at the cliffs marking a former coastline.
The ancient sea cliffs now stand about 5 km inland, forming a border between the coastal lowlands and the Icelandic Highlands.
r1730071533: A mountain chain over 1,500 km long in northern Algeria, forming a natural barrier between the Mediterranean and the Sahara.
Algiers and Oran lie at its base, while Constantine sits directly within the range.
Its highest summit is Lalla Khedidja in the Djurdjura Range.
l1159106851: Canada's eleventh-largest lake, in Manitoba about 300 km northwest of Winnipeg.
Its name is a diminutive of Lake Winnipeg, meaning 'little muddy waters.'
xQ631789: The longest glacier in the world outside the polar regions, in Tajikistan's Pamir Mountains.
Extends about 77 km and reaches up to 1,000 m thick.
r1159102643: A sandstone plateau in northeastern Chad, shaped by wind and temperature erosion within the Sahara.
Home to rock art depicting cattle dating back nearly 7,000 years.
Inhabited seasonally today by semi-nomadic herding communities.
p1159104885: A headland in Somalia's Puntland state, forming the geographical apex of the Horn of Africa.
The second easternmost point on mainland Africa, after Ras Hafun.
Named after the offshore Guardafui Channel.
l1159114237: The fifth largest lake in Sweden and the largest in the central region, in Jämtland County.
Home to Storsjöodjuret, a legendary lake monster similar to the Loch Ness Monster.
The city of Östersund sits on its eastern shore.
vQ2237: A glacier-fed river flowing from the Canadian Rockies to join the South Saskatchewan River, forming the Saskatchewan River.
Its watershed covers most of southern and central Alberta and Saskatchewan.
m1159119271: The estuary outlet of the Delaware River between the states of Delaware and New Jersey.
A designated Ramsar Wetland of International Importance and a major breeding ground for horseshoe crabs.
Crossed by the Cape May-Lewes Ferry.
xQ571430: Covers 98% of the Antarctic continent and holds about 61% of all fresh water on Earth.

r1730072167: A historical region along the Bight of Benin and Bight of Biafra, spanning parts of Togo, Benin and Nigeria.

r1159104197: A major mountain range in western North America, running from the Yukon through British Columbia's coast to the Fraser River.

m1159119247: A bay on the Gulf of Maine along the central Massachusetts coastline.

r1159103553: A mountain system in northeastern Siberia's Magadan Oblast, along the Sea of Okhotsk.

p1159104973: The southwesternmost point of Portugal and of mainland Europe, in the Algarve.

r1159103581: A mountain range in western Myanmar, separating Rakhine State's coast from the Irrawaddy River basin.

r1159104097: A plateau region in the eastern US, between the Atlantic Plain and the Blue Ridge Mountains.

r1159103645: A dry lake bed in northern Utah, between the Great Salt Lake and the Nevada border.

xQ37545: A four-tiered waterfall on the Mahadayi River in Goa, India, among the country's tallest waterfalls.

r1159104619: A rocky peninsula on New Zealand's South Island, formed by two now-extinct volcanoes.

xQ5683183: A waterfall on Havasu Creek within the Grand Canyon, Arizona.
